scope: Route the immediate requested deliverable. Recording a future investigation is note-taking, not doing that investigation. For mixed requests, consider only the hardest required current action. Use a project brief only where it changes that action; unrelated architecture must not inflate a routine task. Project/workspace selection does not turn a greeting into project implementation. Route only the immediate ask; hello, hi, thanks and other simple social exchanges use Luna low unless the ask also requests teaching or substantive work.
model: Luna follows previously established, documented, repeatable flows: notes, copies, exact retrieval, standard metadata checks and routine media edits. It should execute an existing method, not invent the workflow or lay a new implementation/polish foundation. Sol handles foundation design, bespoke implementation, synthesis, nuanced review and interacting contracts. Standard metadata removal is conventional; judging sensitive visible/audio content needs Sol. Missing inputs or a new filename alone do not make an established operation foundation work. For this WebUI, treat Luna as the lower-capability model that generally gives lower-quality responses than Sol 6.1, especially for depth, nuance and teaching. Prefer gpt-6.1-sol when the user wants to learn something new, asks to be taught, requests an explanation, or asks how something functions or why it works. Educational quality takes priority over a short or apparently simple question. Luna remains suitable for exact retrieval and established repeatable execution when teaching or conceptual understanding is not the requested deliverable. Simple greetings, thanks, acknowledgements and casual social exchanges use gpt-6-luna; the quality preference for learning does not apply to a bare greeting.
effort: Choose effort separately from model strength. Sol low can handle complex execution with a known approach and direct checks. Establishing new architecture, reusable flows or a polish baseline tends toward Sol high: early decisions shape later work. Medium can suffice when those decisions are already fixed; use xhigh for deep unresolved constraints. Raise effort for uncertain methods, competing hypotheses, difficult correctness or likely plan revisions. Length, repetition and runtime are not effort. Unknown referents can warrant provisional medium; do not invent work. Effort does not limit persistence or retries.

preparation: Assess online search benefit, need for up-to-date external facts, and project context separately from model/effort. Apply these diagnostics to every automatic classification, including Luna low. Current prices, tools and libraries may need fresh verification; follow-up references may need a maintained project summary. A selected project alone does not make a greeting need context. Recording a future investigation is note-taking. These answers are advisory and do not prove retrieval occurred.
